newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Insolvent firms on rise in Yugo - institute.
newsitem.headline: Insolvent firms on rise in Yugo - institute.

text.p: The number of insolvent Yugoslav firms increases each month and is a big burden to the country's economic recovery, the Belgrade-based Institute for Market Research (IZIT) said on Wednesday.
"An enormous number of permanently insolvent firms make it difficult to maintain the production process," Tomislav Milisavljevic of the IZIT told Reuters.
"They have particularly negative effects on the efforts to boost production and exports," he said.
According to IZIT's latest monthly report, number of insolvent firms was on the rise in the year to end-September and reached 21,486, up from 20,530 insolvent firms in August.
These firms employ 632,000 people out of total number of 2,065 million employed in September.
Their due but unpaid liabilities in September stood at 4.452 billion dinars ($890 million), up 1.9 percent compared to the previous month.
The institute of financial rehabilitation and liquidation of insolvent firms has not functioned well so far, said Milisavljevic.

Out of 21,486 insolvent firms, a proposal has been made to place into receivership 18,525 or 86 percent of the firms which employ 427,500 workers. These firms owed 3.968 billion dinars (about $794 million)
"This represents about 89 percent of the entire internal debt," Milisavljevic said.
Receivership procedure has been instituted for only 1,469 firms employing 19,440 workers and it has been concluded for only 260 firms, he said.
" The problem with insolvent firms is that although they represent a small percentage of total number of firms, they employ an enormous number of people," Milisavljevic said.

"Most of the insolvent firms are big ones with a huge labour surplus," he added. "Although speedier liquidation of insolvent firms will increase unemployment, it is a must if we want our economy to recover." -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
